conclusions: All cold/carried n0 elements match official. The selected original increasing-K FP32 fmaf plus original FP32 bias then BF16 recipe exactly reproduces all four stored candidate qr outputs.

Terminal BF16 conversion is consistent with ties-to-even. Cold first biased value0x3cb48000 is a BF16 midpoint; cold worst0x3fec8008 lies above midpoint0x3fec8000; carried worst0xbf217ffe lies on the opposite side of midpoint0xbf218000. Tiny accumulated FP32 differences survive cancellation with bias and alter terminal BF16.

Exact rational dot plus unchanged bias matches the saved official BF16 projection for both cold selected outputs and carried worst output, but not carried first output. Small-shape Torch Linear also differs from the original full-matrix official capture at carried first output. Full original backend accumulation therefore remains unmeasured.

Rounding dot to BF16 before bias is only a counterfactual control, is not applied to candidate, and fails to reproduce the original official first projection differences. It is not established as an official bias policy.

Cold worst valid score and carried worst valid score are explained locally by one changed Q element with identical K. Using saved official Q in the candidate16-stripe selected-cell operator recovers the stored official scores; this is a counterfactual local attribution, not an accepted alternate reference.

Carried first valid score difference has bit-identical Q and K: candidate C and selected small-shape Torch produce53, stored original full-shape official produces52.75. Candidate and exact-dot FP32 are0x44158001 (598.00006103515625), then BF16dot600. The original pre-scale matmul output is not captured here, so the exact full-shape backend reduction cause remains unresolved.

Official self-cache and actual-cache-conditioned Q,K,scores,logits are bit-identical in the stored carried captures. Their V-cache prefix differs and downstream attention/residual differs; these paths must not be conflated.
